independent.summary: Escape closes the drawer but never clears `activeOptions` or the rendered pills, so the document-level quick-reply hotkey handler (line 814, guarded only by `!activeOptions || e.target === input`) stays armed with the widget closed: after Escape with Yes/No pills showing, pressing `y`/`n` (or `1`-`4` for a numbered set) anywhere on the host page — including into the host's own input fields, since `e.target` is not the widget's input — is `preventDefault()`ed and silently POSTs that option to `/chat`. The new smoke assertion at smoke.mjs:340 cements the leaked state by asserting the pills stay in place.

`aria-modal="true"` is added to `#leo-drawer` while a focus trap is explicitly out of scope, which is the one combination the attribute must not be used in: assistive tech responds to `aria-modal` by restricting virtual navigation to the dialog subtree, so for a non-modal floating chat widget appended to `document.body` the entire host page becomes unreachable to screen-reader users for as long as the drawer is open, while keyboard Tab still walks focus out into that now-hidden content. Previously `role="dialog"` alone imposed no such restriction, so this is a net regression for the users the item targets.

`aria-live="polite"` is put on `#leo-messages`, which is also the container that history is bulk-inserted into (`loadHistory` inserts up to 20 messages plus a greeting on open, and prepends another 20 on scroll-to-top at line 429), and the container `setLoading` appends the `…` typing bubble to. Opening the drawer therefore makes the screen reader queue the whole restored transcript rather than just Leo's new reply, and every send announces a bare ellipsis; the announcement target needed to be scoped to newly arrived assistant messages (or suppressed during history load).

The assertion "Escape while options are showing sends no message — the hotkey path did not fire" cannot fail for the reason it names: the hotkey handler only matches `y`/`n` or `parseInt(e.key)` in 1..options.length, and `parseInt('Escape')` is `NaN`, so Escape could never reach `selectOption` before or after this change. It guards nothing about handler ordering or the new Escape listener, despite the item requesting it as a regression check.
